name: The Universe
description: The universe itself: the Big Bang, galaxies, stars, black holes and the planets, and the theories and discoveries that showed how it all began and works.

checkpoints.name: The early universe
checkpoints.note: The universe begins in the Big Bang and swells in a split second. Within a few hundred million years the first stars and galaxies shine and the Milky Way forms. Generations of stars forge the elements that planets and people are made of.

checkpoints.name: The Sun and its planets
checkpoints.note: A cloud of gas and dust collapses into the Sun and a disk around it. Rock and ice clump into planets, a collision makes our Moon, and the leftovers become the asteroid belt, the comets and the Kuiper belt.

checkpoints.name: Watching the sky
checkpoints.note: Babylonians, Greeks, Chinese, Indians and the Maya chart the sky by eye and predict eclipses. Ptolemy puts the Earth at the centre of everything, and Chinese astronomers record a new star in 1054.

checkpoints.name: The Sun at the centre
checkpoints.note: Copernicus moves the Earth around the Sun, Galileo sees the moons of Jupiter, Kepler and Newton explain the orbits, and Uranus and Neptune are found.

checkpoints.name: An expanding universe
checkpoints.note: Einstein shows that gravity bends space and time. Hubble finds that other galaxies exist and are rushing away, Lemaître traces it back to a beginning, and dark matter is first suspected.

checkpoints.name: Modern cosmology
checkpoints.note: The afterglow of the Big Bang is found. Pulsars, black holes and planets around other stars are discovered, dark energy is speeding up the expansion, gravitational waves are heard and black holes are photographed.
